candidates.trigger: diff adds a `git archive` invocation in a Gradle release task without a `.gitattributes` export-ignore for `gradle-wrapper.jar`

candidates.rule: Public interfaces in the Java/Kotlin SDK must carry KDoc/JavaDoc so that SDK documentation can be generated from source and IDEs can show inline help.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `public interface` or `public class` to `java-sdk/sdk/src/main/kotlin/` without a KDoc block

candidates.rule: The `execute_complete` method of a deferrable operator must handle every status emitted by its paired Trigger, including `cancelled`; a missing branch silently reports task success for a cancelled job.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a status constant (e.g. `"cancelled"`, `"timeout"`) to a Trigger's `TriggerEvent` yield but the corresponding `execute_complete` in the operator has no branch for that status

candidates.rule: Do not add a `stream()` method stub that raises `NotImplementedError` on a log handler; the log framework uses `getattr` to detect streaming support and the stub defeats the fallback to `read()`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `def stream(self, ...) -> ...: raise NotImplementedError` to a class that also inherits from a remote log handler

candidates.rule: The `tags` field in a provider's `provider.yaml` must match the tags declared in `get_provider_info.py`; mismatched tags produce conflicting categorisation in generated provider docs.
candidates.trigger: diff modifies `provider.yaml` `tags:` or `get_provider_info.py` tags list in a provider package and the two sources no longer agree

candidates.rule: Hooks that accept an `access_type` (or equivalent enum-like parameter) must validate the value against `VALID_*` constants and raise `ValueError` with a message listing allowed values before making any API call.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a hook method that branches on `access_type` / `auth_type` without an explicit `if ... not in VALID_...` guard before the branching

candidates.rule: Provider changelog entries in `changelog.rst` must use sentence-case commit titles (capitalise only the first word and proper nouns); lowercase prefixes such as `fix:` are not acceptable.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a line to `providers/*/docs/changelog.rst` whose commit title starts with a lowercase word or a `fix:`/`feat:` conventional-commit prefix

candidates.rule: When tightening a provider dependency to a `<X.Y` upper bound, leave a recorded note (in code comment or issue) stating the conditions under which the cap can be relaxed.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an upper-bound pin (`<X.Y`) to a provider's dependency in `provider.yaml` or `setup.cfg` without an accompanying comment explaining when the cap may be lifted

candidates.rule: Trigger test cases that verify a specific deadline path (e.g. `execution_deadline`) must set the other deadline (`end_time`) to a future value so each test exercises exactly one timeout branch.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a Trigger unit test where both `end_time` and `execution_deadline` are set to already-expired values

candidates.rule: Do not use `caplog` in Kubernetes/integration tests; replace it with mock-based log capture to avoid test flakiness that CI static checks will flag as a failure.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `caplog` as a parameter or fixture to a test function in `kubernetes-tests/`

candidates.rule: When renaming public executor attributes (e.g. `pending_tasks` → `pending_workloads`), keep the old name as a deprecated property shim that delegates to the new name to preserve back-compat.
candidates.trigger: diff renames an instance attribute or method on a class that subclasses BaseExecutor (e.g. `self.pending_tasks` → `self.pending_workloads`) without adding a `@property` shim

candidates.rule: When renaming public executor methods (e.g. `sync_running_tasks` → `sync_running_workloads`), add a deprecated forwarding wrapper under the old name to preserve back-compat.
candidates.trigger: diff renames a public method on an executor subclass without adding a same-named wrapper method that calls the new name

candidates.rule: When an operator adds a new boolean parameter that controls trigger behavior, the operator must accept and pass that parameter through rather than hard-coding a value in the trigger instantiation.
candidates.trigger: diff instantiates an Airflow trigger with a boolean argument (e.g. `cancel_on_kill=True`) that is not exposed as a parameter on the enclosing operator

candidates.rule: When an operator parameter changes behavior (e.g. `awslogs_enabled` previously controlling log fetching), the new implementation must preserve the parameter's documented effect in both deferrable and non-deferrable code paths.
candidates.trigger: diff refactors deferrable operator execution and leaves a previously-honored parameter (e.g. `awslogs_enabled`) without effect in the `execute_complete` path

candidates.rule: For CloudWatch / external-resource operator links, persist links that require job completion (e.g. log stream ARN) after the job completes, not before, in the non-deferrable path.
candidates.trigger: diff calls `_persist_links()` or equivalent before `hook.wait_for_job()` in a non-deferrable execute path where the link data is only available post-completion

candidates.rule: When changing behavior covered by existing tests, update tests to explicitly cover both the new branch and any removed/altered branch; do not leave tests asserting old behavior that no longer applies.
candidates.trigger: diff changes conditional logic in an AWS operator (e.g. `awslogs_enabled` branch) without adding or updating unit tests for both the enabled and disabled paths

candidates.rule: Amazon provider operator docstrings must tag templatable parameters with `(templated)` in the parameter description.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a new parameter docstring line in an Amazon provider operator, trigger, or sensor without appending `(templated)` to the description of a parameter that is listed in `template_fields`

candidates.rule: AWS operator `execute()` return values should be minimal, meaningful identifiers (e.g. ARN, URI, name) rather than raw, full boto3 response dicts.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `return response` (the raw boto3 response dict) as the final statement of an AWS operator's `execute()` method

candidates.rule: Removing a parameter that controls waiter policy selection is a breaking change; instead, deprecate the old parameter and map its values to the new parameter.
candidates.trigger: diff removes a parameter (e.g. `wait_policy`) from an EMR operator and hard-codes one of its former values, silently eliminating other valid enum values

candidates.rule: Provider operator RST how-to docs must order lifecycle sections to reflect the natural resource lifecycle (Create → Start → Stop → Update → Delete).
candidates.trigger: diff adds a new RST section in a provider how-to doc where the section order does not follow the resource lifecycle sequence

candidates.rule: When documenting a constraint (e.g. maximum list size) in an operator's docstring, enforce that constraint with a runtime check in `__init__`; do not document bounds that are not validated.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a docstring stating a numeric bound (e.g. "maximum 200") for a parameter but `__init__` does not validate that bound

candidates.rule: When a provider imports a type from airflow-core that does not yet exist in the minimum supported core version, gate the import behind a runtime version check rather than importing it unconditionally.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an unconditional import of a symbol from `airflow.executors.workloads.types` or a similarly new airflow-core module in a provider that targets an older min_ver

candidates.rule: In `BaseExecutor._process_workloads` and its overrides, name the sequence parameter `workload_items` (not `workloads`) to avoid shadowing the `airflow.executors.workloads` module import.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or modifies a method with a parameter named `workloads` in an executor subclass where `from airflow.executors import workloads` is also imported

candidates.rule: AWS executor failures must not log each individual failure inline; they must be aggregated and logged once at the summary point to avoid spam.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `self.log.info(…)` or `self.log.error(…)` inside a per-task failure branch in an AWS executor's sync loop

candidates.rule: AWS hooks that use a Boto3 client must subclass the appropriate Boto-specific base class (e.g. `AwsBaseHook`), not the generic `BaseHook`.
candidates.trigger: diff introduces a new AWS hook that imports from `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk` to get `BaseHook` while also creating a Boto3 client

candidates.rule: Do not raise `AirflowException` for failures that are not caused by Airflow itself; use the most appropriate Python built-in exception instead.
candidates.trigger: diff raises `AirflowException` for a non-Airflow-infrastructure failure (e.g. an external service returning an unexpected state, bad user input)

candidates.rule: In deferrable operators, call `self.persist()` (or equivalent link/metadata persistence) before `self.defer()`, because `defer()` raises `TaskDeferred` making every subsequent line unreachable.
candidates.trigger: diff places a `self.persist(…)` or XCom push or operator-link-persist call after a `self.defer(…)` call in the same code path

candidates.rule: In `execute_complete`, never fall back to `self.<attribute>` set during `execute`; read all required state exclusively from the trigger event dict.
candidates.trigger: diff uses `self.job_id` (or any attribute set in `execute`) inside `execute_complete` as a fallback when the event dict does not contain the value

candidates.rule: In `execute_complete`, always check `event["status"]` and raise on error before treating the event as a success.
candidates.trigger: diff implements `execute_complete` and reads payload fields from `event` without first checking `event["status"]` for an error value

candidates.rule: Do not replace AirflowException with RuntimeError in operator/sensor/trigger error paths without auditing all callers that catch the original exception type.
candidates.trigger: diff removes `raise AirflowException(` and adds `raise RuntimeError(` inside an operator, sensor, or trigger

candidates.rule: In async trigger `run()` methods, define and explicitly handle distinct SUCCESS and FAILURE terminal states; do not collapse all non-transitional statuses into a single success event.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an `async def run()` trigger that yields a `TriggerEvent` without separate success/failure state handling, or compares status against a single string instead of an Enum

candidates.rule: Avoid redundant unit tests that exercise the same code paths as more complex tests already present; prefer fewer, higher-value tests over exhaustive branch-by-branch coverage.
candidates.trigger: diff adds multiple small test functions each testing a single simple branch that is also exercised as a sub-case of an existing broader test in the same file

candidates.rule: In caplog-based trigger tests, call `caplog.set_level("INFO")` before invoking the method under test to prevent environment-dependent log-capture failures.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an `async def test_*` that calls a trigger method and then asserts on `caplog.records` or `caplog.text` without first setting `caplog.set_level(...)`

candidates.rule: Prefer using the provider's existing Hook class (e.g., `KafkaProducerHook`) rather than constructing the underlying client directly inside operator or listener code.
candidates.trigger: diff constructs a provider client (e.g., `confluent_kafka.Producer(...)`) directly inside operator, trigger, or listener code where a corresponding Hook already wraps that client

candidates.rule: Trigger resource-holder attributes (e.g., a consumer or client stored on `self`) must be initialised to `None` in `__init__` and reset to `None` after cleanup to make the cleanup method idempotent.
candidates.trigger: diff assigns `self.<resource>` for the first time inside `async def run()` (or another non-`__init__` method) of a `BaseTrigger` subclass

candidates.rule: New provider dependencies (e.g., `requests`) used in provider source code must be declared in the provider's `pyproject.toml` before the code that uses them is merged.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `import <package>` inside `providers/<name>/src/` where `<package>` is not listed as a dependency in `providers/<name>/pyproject.toml`

candidates.rule: Operator parameters that are initialised in `__init__` must be declared as constructor arguments; do not reference `self.<param>` in `execute()` if the parameter was never added to `__init__`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a reference to `self.<param>` inside `execute()` or `execute_complete()` of an operator where the same `<param>` is not present in the class `__init__` signature

candidates.rule: State-tracking attributes that represent submission/execution status must be initialised in `__init__` and must not be reset inside the method that drives the operation (e.g., `submit()`).
candidates.trigger: diff assigns a state-tracking attribute (e.g., `self._yarn_application_submitted = False`) at the top of an operation method (`submit`, `execute`, `run`) rather than in `__init__`

candidates.rule: In `SparkSubmitHook.submit()`, post-submit commands or cleanup called after the job completes must be wrapped in a `try/finally` block so they execute regardless of whether the job succeeded or failed.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a method call (e.g., `self._run_post_submit_commands()`) after an `AirflowException` raise site inside `SparkSubmitHook.submit()` without a `try/finally` guard

candidates.rule: Spark provider documentation for K8s-API tracking must note that the worker's kube client is used for pod tracking and that the K8s path bypasses `ResumableJobMixin`, causing retries to submit a fresh driver instead of reattaching.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or modifies a **Requirements** or **Caveats** section for K8s-based Spark submission in `providers/apache/spark/docs/`

candidates.rule: Spark provider documentation describing failure modes must note that conflicts can arise when a resubmitted job is not idempotent, not only that compute is wasted.
candidates.trigger: diff adds prose about worker-crash / job-resubmission behaviour in `providers/apache/spark/docs/` without mentioning idempotency conflicts

candidates.rule: Use the provider-specific Enum (e.g., `DmsTaskWaiterStatus`) for state comparisons inside triggers and operators instead of raw string literals.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a comparison like `if status != "<state_string>"` inside a trigger or operator where a corresponding Enum already exists in the provider

candidates.rule: Inside async trigger methods (including `safe_to_cancel()`), wrap synchronous DB/hook calls with `sync_to_async()` to prevent blocking the triggerer event loop.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a synchronous call (e.g., `self.get_task_instance()`, `hook.stop_query()`) inside an `async def` method of a `BaseTrigger` subclass without `await sync_to_async(...)`

candidates.rule: In system tests, set `AIRFLOW_CONN_*` environment variables inside a `@task`-decorated function rather than at DAG parse time, so the connection is available in the same worker process that executes subsequent tasks.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `os.environ[f"AIRFLOW_CONN_..."] = ...` at DAG-level scope (outside any `@task`) in a system test file

candidates.rule: System tests must annotate each task chain step with its phase: setup, test body, or teardown—mirroring the pattern used in canonical examples such as `example_sqs.py`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `chain(...)` call in a system test file without inline comments or task naming that distinguishes setup / test / teardown phases

candidates.rule: System tests must be validated by running them locally before submission; reviewers will reject system tests that have not been exercised end-to-end.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or substantially modifies a file matching `providers/*/tests/system/**/*.py`

candidates.rule: In system test DAGs, read external variables (e.g., role ARNs from `SystemTestContextBuilder`) and perform connection setup inside a `@task`-decorated function so XCom resolution happens at task runtime, not at DAG-parse time.
candidates.trigger: diff adds code that reads `os.environ[<VAR>]` or constructs a connection string at module/DAG-definition scope in a system test file

candidates.rule: In `pytest.raises` blocks that test a specific AWS `ClientError` error code, add a `match=` parameter to assert the exact error code rather than any `ClientError`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `pytest.raises(ClientError)` without a `match=` argument in a provider unit test

candidates.rule: Remove unused `moto` fixtures and their associated `mock_aws` imports from unit tests; do not leave moto infrastructure in a test module that does not exercise real AWS API calls.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `@pytest.fixture` that wraps a hook with `mock_aws()` context manager but the fixture is not referenced by any test function in the same module

candidates.rule: When implementing Kerberos auth resolution in a Spark provider hook, include the krb5ccache path alongside keytab/principal so REST calls to a Kerberized YARN RM always carry an Authorization header.
candidates.trigger: A method returns auth object based on `keytab` and `principal` connection fields but omits a branch for `_use_krb5ccache` or equivalent ccache flag.

candidates.rule: Do not add module-level private constants to a provider module unless they are referenced in that module; dead constants must be wired in or removed.
candidates.trigger: A new `_SOME_CONF = "..."` constant is introduced at module level in a provider file but has no call-site reference within the same diff.

candidates.rule: ImportError compatibility shims for Task SDK symbols must carry a `>=X.Y.Z` version marker in a comment, referencing the minimum SDK/Airflow release that introduced the symbol.
candidates.trigger: A `try: from airflow.sdk... except ImportError: Symbol = None` block is added without a comment specifying the minimum version that exports the symbol.

candidates.rule: When a broad `except Exception` handler wraps code that deliberately raises `AirflowException`, re-raise `AirflowException` unchanged before the generic handler to preserve the intended error message.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces a specific `raise AirflowException(...)` inside a `try` block that also has a downstream `except Exception as e` that re-wraps or swallows the exception.

candidates.rule: Prose notes and warnings in provider changelog RST files must use the RST `.. note::` or `.. warning::` directive, not plain prose, so they render correctly in the documentation site.
candidates.trigger: A provider `docs/changelog.rst` diff adds a paragraph that reads as a note or warning without a leading `.. note::` or `.. warning::` RST directive.

candidates.rule: Documentation claims about KubernetesPodOperator deduplication or ambiguity prevention must be scoped to the specific code path (e.g. `get_or_create_pod`) where the guarantee holds, not asserted end-to-end.
candidates.trigger: A diff to a provider `docs/` RST file claims "no possibility of ambiguity failure" or equivalent absolute language for pod reconnect behaviour.

candidates.rule: New parameters added to `KubernetesPodOperator.__init__` must have a matching docstring entry describing the parameter type; for `Callable` parameters the docstring must name each positional argument's meaning.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a new keyword argument to `KubernetesPodOperator.__init__` (or any `*Operator.__init__` in the cncf.kubernetes provider) without a corresponding `:param name:` entry in the class docstring.

candidates.rule: XCom push guards in KubernetesPodOperator must use `if value is not None` rather than `if value` (or `if not value`) so that falsy values such as `0`, `False`, or empty string are persisted correctly.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces `if not value:` or `if value:` as a guard before an XCom push call inside `KubernetesPodOperator` (or its mixins).

candidates.rule: When persisting pod identity to the task state store, either verify the stored `uid` against the live pod on reconnect or omit `uid` from the stored payload so the schema does not imply verification that is not performed.
candidates.trigger: A diff stores `uid` alongside `name`/`namespace` in a task-state-store payload for pod identity, but the reconnect code only uses `name`/`namespace` without comparing `pod.metadata.uid` to the stored uid.

candidates.rule: When a parameter's behaviour is gated on a minimum Airflow version, its docstring must state the version constraint explicitly (e.g. "Only available for Airflow 3.3+").
candidates.trigger: A new operator parameter is introduced whose full behaviour requires Airflow ≥X.Y but the `:param name:` docstring entry omits the version constraint.

candidates.rule: When replacing a deprecated parameter with a new version-gated one, silently translate the deprecated parameter's value for users below the minimum required version rather than forcing them to change parameter names.
candidates.trigger: A diff deprecates parameter A and introduces replacement parameter B that only works on Airflow ≥X.Y, without fallback logic that makes B behave like A when the runtime version is below X.Y.

candidates.rule: Kubernetes field selectors using comma-separated `!=` expressions must be verified to produce the correct Boolean semantics (`NOT A AND NOT B`, not `NOT (A OR B)`) before merging.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces a Kubernetes field selector string of the form `status.phase!=X,status.phase!=Y` where the intent is to exclude pods in either state X or state Y.

candidates.rule: Failures in Kubernetes driver-pod deletion must not propagate as task errors; wrap `_delete_driver_pod()` calls with `contextlib.suppress` or a flag that downgrades the error to a warning.
candidates.trigger: A call to `_delete_driver_pod()` or equivalent pod-cleanup method appears inline in a polling loop without error suppression or a configurable error-vs-warning flag.

candidates.rule: Do not change the default value of an existing operator or hook parameter that affects pre-existing code paths; new code paths may enforce their own floor via `max()` but the legacy default must stay unchanged.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes the default of an `__init__` parameter (e.g. `status_poll_interval`) that was already used by a pre-existing execution path, not only by the newly introduced path.

candidates.rule: When calling the Spark Standalone REST submission API, check the `success` field before accessing `driverState`; raise with the response's `message` field on failure.
candidates.trigger: Code accesses `response.json()["driverState"]` from a Spark Standalone REST response without first asserting `response.json()["success"] is True`.

candidates.rule: Do not land unreachable code branches in a PR; either drop scaffolding branches or mark them with a TODO referencing the specific follow-up PR that will make them reachable.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces `if self._hook._is_yarn:` or similar runtime-gated branches that are never reachable from any entry-point added in the same PR.

candidates.rule: Spark provider REST calls must derive scheme (http/https) and port from Airflow connection extras rather than hardcoding `http://` and a fixed port number.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces a `requests.get(f"http://{host}:<hardcoded_port>/...")` call inside a Spark provider operator or hook.

candidates.rule: Transient HTTP calls inside provider status-polling loops must be wrapped with a retry strategy (e.g. `tenacity`) to avoid burning a task retry slot on a one-second network blip.
candidates.trigger: A `requests.get(...)` or similar HTTP call appears inside a polling loop (e.g. inside `get_job_status`, `poll_until_complete`) with no retry/backoff wrapper.

candidates.rule: Provider changelogs must not include a release entry when only test files or non-functional pyproject.toml marker comments were modified in the PR.
candidates.trigger: A diff to a provider's `docs/changelog.rst` adds a new version section for a PR whose only changed files are under `tests/` or contain only `# use next version` comments in `pyproject.toml`.

candidates.rule: CLI commands in providers must raise `SystemExit` (not `AirflowConfigException`) for user-facing configuration errors, consistent with other CLI argument validation.
candidates.trigger: A `raise AirflowConfigException(...)` or `raise AirflowException(...)` appears inside a CLI command function (functions decorated or called from `airflow/cli/` or provider `cli/` modules).

candidates.rule: Provider secrets-backend classes must only implement methods declared in BaseSecretsBackend; do not add extra public methods (e.g. get_config) that are absent from the base class interface.
candidates.trigger: A class extending BaseSecretsBackend defines a public method not present in airflow/secrets/base_secrets.py

candidates.rule: Remove manual ImportError guards for airflow-core symbols that are already handled by airflow.providers.common.compat; the compat layer itself provides the AF2/AF3 fallback.
candidates.trigger: A provider module contains try/except ImportError around an import that airflow.providers.common.compat already redirects

candidates.rule: Provider hook methods that map Airflow connection extras to a third-party library's kwargs must use truthiness filtering (if extra.get(k)) not identity checks (is not None), so that empty-string UI values fall through to environment-based auth.
candidates.trigger: A provider hook builds kwargs from connection extras using {k: extra[k] for k in keys if extra.get(k) is not None}

candidates.rule: Provider hook connection-extra field names must match the exact parameter names accepted by the target library; document the mapping if names differ and convert or load the value before passing it.
candidates.trigger: A provider hook passes a connection extra key directly to a third-party constructor without verifying the parameter name matches the library's API (e.g. project_id vs project, service_account_file vs credentials object)

candidates.rule: Reuse shared exception types from providers/standard/exceptions.py (e.g. HITLRejectException) rather than defining per-provider duplicates for the same semantic error.
candidates.trigger: A provider defines a new exception class whose docstring or purpose duplicates an existing exception in providers/standard/exceptions.py

candidates.rule: Do not expose operator or mixin parameters in __init__ and docstrings unless they are fully implemented; stub parameters that have no effect must be removed or replaced with a NotImplementedError/warning until the feature ships.
candidates.trigger: An operator stores a parameter via self.param = param in __init__ but the parameter is never read by any method in the same class or its mixins

candidates.rule: bytes fields must not be included in template_fields; Jinja renders bytes as their repr string (b'...'), causing AttributeError on .decode() and passing literal repr text to binary parsers.

candidates.rule: Operators that build prompts or strings incrementally must not embed the accumulator variable in its own f-string; construct the string linearly from separate parts to avoid duplication.

candidates.rule: Provider operator methods that iterate over connection IDs must use a cached hook property (e.g. self._db_hooks[conn_id]) rather than constructing a new hook on every call to avoid redundant connections.
candidates.trigger: A method loops over connection IDs and calls a factory function like self._get_db_hook(conn_id) inside the loop when a cached property (_db_hooks) already exists on the class

candidates.rule: In Kubernetes-provider tests, mock V1Pod status with V1PodStatus(...) objects, not plain dicts, so that serialization via to_dict() matches real API behaviour.
candidates.trigger: Test code assigns pod.status = {"key": value} instead of pod.status = V1PodStatus(...)

candidates.rule: Use time_machine to freeze time in tests that compare timestamps or durations; do not compute expected values relative to datetime.datetime.now().

candidates.rule: When writing pod-selection tests for SparkKubernetesOperator, keep metadata.name identical across all test pods and set deletion_timestamp explicitly so the selection criteria are each independently exercised.

candidates.rule: Provider documentation that exposes only a subset of an upstream library's capabilities must link to the upstream capability list and note which features are not yet supported.

candidates.rule: Full runnable DAGs in provider documentation must be included via '.. exampleinclude::' referencing a tested file under example_dags/; inline '.. code-block:: python' is reserved for code fragments only.
candidates.trigger: A provider .rst file contains a '.. code-block:: python' block that is a complete, runnable DAG rather than a fragment

candidates.rule: Example DAGs must set schedule=None explicitly; do not omit the schedule parameter in provider example_dags files.

candidates.rule: Provider factory classes whose keys are enum members must type-annotate the mapping as dict[EnumType, ...] and accept both str and the enum in public entry points, normalising strings to enum values with an informative ValueError.

candidates.rule: Do not explicitly set trigger_rule='all_success' on @task or Operator; it is the default and its presence implies non-standard behaviour to readers.
